title: Locked paired validation of closed-loop therapy software: controller rankings are not robust to analysis choices
description:
Reproducibility package for a PeerJ Computer Science Research Article. The study evaluates four delayed-feedback controllers for coupled photothermal-photodynamic simulation against delayed full feedback under a locked, paired, multiplicity-controlled protocol.

The package contains the trial-level locked validation atlas (4,608 paired trials per controller, 384 clusters), the frozen predicted-baseline-success scoring rule, the cluster-robust inference pipeline (10,000-replicate cluster bootstrap, 20,000-vector sign-flip permutation tests, Holm correction, minimum detectable effects at 80% power), a 16-specification curve per controller, Pareto dominance analysis and a 200,000-draw Dirichlet weight-sensitivity analysis, together with the manuscript source and build.

Headline result: no controller improves overall success. The apparent benefit in the predicted-low stratum (+0.031 to +0.056) does not survive Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.629 in every case). All four controllers are Pareto non-dominated, and the sign of the headline effect changes across defensible analysis specifications for three of the four controllers.
